financing.summary: Private, family- and employee-owned builder (Bright Industries family; ESOP since 2017) with no SEC filings and no public debt, so its credit lines, lenders and lot counts are not public. Its model is to buy developer-finished lots in third-party master-planned communities in DFW and on the Colorado Front Range (Hillwood, at Treeline, is the named developer partner), plus lots in the family's own Castle Hills (Bright Realty). There is no public land-banking or lot-option partner and no public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon. The parent's balance sheet (Bright Industries, a diversified real-estate and energy family company) is the most likely funding backstop, which may reduce the need for outside land capital; equally, a builder of about 600 closings a year that buys finished lots from developers on takedown schedules is a natural lot-option prospect. The one land decision-maker is Forrest Hartley.
financing.land_strategy: Buys finished homesites in master-planned communities from outside developers; the company credits long-standing developer relationships and fast response to new opportunities for its growth (CEO Kevin Egan, Dec 2022). No owned-versus-optioned target is published. Also builds in Castle Hills, developed by affiliate Bright Realty.

land_banking.description: Sister company under Bright Industries that developed the 2,900-acre Castle Hills master plan in Lewisville; ALH is building townhomes in Castle Hills Northpointe, described as the community's final phase. A captive lot source, terms not public.
land_banking.source_title: The DFW Financial Unicorn: ... Final Phase of Castle Hills (company blog, 2026-11-19)
land_banking.note: Bright Realty describes Castle Hills on https://www.brightrealty.com/about. Not a land-banking arrangement; recorded as the affiliate lot source.

land_banking.description: Lot seller in Treeline (Justin, TX); ALH says it builds in several Hillwood communities, naming Treeline. The same post names Ramble (Celina) and Landmark (Denton) as upcoming Hillwood communities but does not say ALH builds there.
land_banking.source_title: Celebrating Success: Treeline Developer Hillwood Communities Shines in 2025 (company blog, 2025-05-29)
land_banking.note: Developer lot-purchase relationship, not a land bank; lot counts and takedown terms not public.
